headline: US envoys meet Putin, Zelensky for Ukraine peace talks, no breakthrough reported
summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held "highly useful" talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and "substantive" discussions with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky regarding a peace settlement. No immediate breakthrough was announced.
details: Russian President Vladimir Putin held over three hours of "highly useful" talks with two US envoys on Saturday evening, seeking a deal to end the Ukraine war. A Kremlin aide stated no breakthrough was indicated.

Envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner "outlined a number of ideas regarding possible avenues for a settlement." Putin told them Russia was making "real progress" on the battlefield and was confident of achieving its goals, stressing the necessity of addressing "all the root causes of the conflict."

These statements align with Moscow's repeated remarks since the full-scale invasion in February 2022. Both sides have intensified long-range air strikes in recent weeks, while front lines remain largely static.
A White House official described the talks as "substantive" and indicated that next steps would be announced in the coming weeks.

Witkoff and Kushner flew from Moscow to Kyiv to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Zelensky announced the first round of talks between Ukraine and US negotiators was over, with Witkoff stating discussions would continue "as long as it takes."

Putin had promised to ensure the safety of the US negotiators, with Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirming an order not to strike Kyiv for three days during their trip. Meanwhile, Ukrainian drones struck an oil refinery in Ryazan and other Russian cities overnight.

In the preceding 10 days, Russia had pounded the Ukrainian capital day and night with missiles and drones. Putin also praised former US President Trump's efforts to end the war, stating he "does not stop his efforts to help bring about a settlement."

headline_marked: [[Amazon cargo plane skids off runway]] onto road in Miami, 5 killed
headline: Amazon cargo plane skids off runway onto road in Miami, 5 killed
summary: The plane struck several vehicles on the road, resulting in five fatalities and at least five serious injuries. Miami International Airport operations were temporarily halted following the incident.
details: A cargo plane skidded off a runway at Miami International Airport in Florida, USA, crashing onto an adjacent road. The aircraft struck several vehicles on the road, resulting in five fatalities and at least five serious injuries.
Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava confirmed the death toll and injuries during a press conference. She did not disclose the names or identities of the victims.
Local media identified the aircraft as a Boeing 767-300 cargo plane operated by Amazon's Prime Air, a world-renowned e-commerce giant.

The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) reported the accident occurred around 2 PM local time on Sunday. The plane had departed from Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, Puerto Rico, en route to Miami.

The FAA further stated that the cargo plane veered off the runway during landing and collided with "multiple" vehicles on the adjacent road before catching fire. Local Fire Rescue authorities described significant flames and extensive smoke at the scene.
Following the incident, operations at Miami International Airport were temporarily suspended.
The exact reason why the cargo plane veered off the runway during landing remains unknown. The precise number of vehicles struck by the aircraft on the road has also not yet been determined.

Kelly Nantele, Director of Corporate Global Media Relations at Amazon, stated that the company is working closely with local authorities and officials to understand the full circumstances of the incident.
